newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- T-bond volatilities ebb, interest in July.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- T-bond volatilities ebb, interest in July.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were generally weaker as the underlying bond market made modest gains in a follow-through to Friday's rally, dealers said.

Although August options were to be the lead-month contract for T-bond futures options on the Chicago Board of Trade, most of the activity was in July options, which expire at the end of the week and are rich in gamma, they added.
"A lot of them are (cleaning up positions in July) and a lot of them are just taking a shot to see if we can get a quick move," said a brokerage firm trader at the CBOT.

Short-dated options have higher gamma, which provides them bigger delta swings for delta-neutral volatility traders and rapid price acceleration against movements in the underlying market. But such options are also vulnerable to time decay.
"With only a week left, people were kind of buying lottery tickets," the CBOT trader said.
Traders said there was a fairly good flow of economic indicators this week, kicking off with Tuesday's May consumer price index, to provoke gamma interest.
One firm was said to have bought 3,000 to 5,000 lots of July 111-112 put spread and 2,000 of 111-113 call spread.
A second firm was seen buying 2,000 of the 113 calls.

However, T-bond futures in the past few months have had a notorious tendency to narrowly gravitate toward the strike price where expiring options had high levels of open interest. Futures hovered near 108 for days ahead of the May expiration and spent weeks around 110 for June options last month.

For July options, the 112 strike had the lion's share of open interest with 40,340 contracts for calls and 2,943 for puts at the end of Friday's session. The 111 strike had 28,763 lots for calls and 10,870 for puts, while 113 had 11,673 for calls and just 41 for puts.
September T-bond futures were up 10/32 on the day at 112-5/32 in late trade, climbing slightly above Friday's 112-2/32 high.

A second CBOT trader said the bond market could be due for some consolidation after recent rallies. Although he did not subscribe to the theory that the 112 strike might have a magnetic effect because of options, he thought pullbacks here would probably minor.
Implied volatility for August T-bond futures options was trading at around 8.1 in late trade, off about 0.2 point on the day, while September stood at 8.3 percent, off 0.1.
Implied volatility for July was choppy because of the short maturity, but traders put it at just above 7.0 percent.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, volatilities for Eurodollar futures options on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange were narrowly mixed.
Implied volatility for December Eurodollars was unchanged at 10.0 percent.
